answer: Submissions that land within 270 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The pigment detector writes to jade, and juniper reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 92 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 2 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
